text:
support: Heads up — NimbusMaps (acct NM-22) opened an escalation (INC-9876). p99 for POST /v1/generate jumped from ~650ms to ~4.8s starting ~2026-03-15 22:10 UTC. They also saw intermittent 500s and a few 401s on retries. trace=tx-9a8b. Log snippet:

[WARN] 2026-03-15T22:10:12Z request_id=tx-9a8b hold_ms=102 batch_size=1 latency=4890ms
[ERROR] 2026-03-15T22:10:12Z downstream=upstream-gen status=502

Customer says it started immediately after some config rollouts last night. Can eng-sre triage?

maria: On it. Any recent rollouts touching continuous batching/coalesce/grace window?

aj: I rolled out "continuous-coalesce-v2" canary at 21:45 UTC. As part of the change the default grace_ms was bumped from 20 -> 100ms to reduce cold start cost. Canary target was ~15% traffic (mostly hosted).

tara: 100ms default for tiny prompts can easily blow up p99 — small reqs get held for longer, then downstream single-request batches still incur full hold. Are NimbusMaps requests small?

support: NimbusMaps typical prompt size is 8–16 tokens, very chatty, so yes small. They also have a slightly bursty pattern around those times.

samir: Quick mitigation: can we disable batching for NM-22 tenant or enable per-tenant nobatch flag? support, can you force a header? (X-Redwood-NoBatch)

support: We can't change their client headers, but we can flip server-side tenant flags.

maria: I'll flip a tenant-scoped feature flag for NM-22 to bypass coalescing and roll the default back. aj, can you run the flag change and rollback the grace_ms default for the canary?

aj: On it. Commands I'm running now:

```bash
# enable per-tenant bypass for NimbusMaps
rbctl feature set coalesce-v2-nobatch --tenant NM-22 --enable
# reduce default for canary back to safe baseline
rbctl rollout feature continuous-coalesce-v2 --percent 10 --set-default-grace_ms 20
```

I'll watch the metric stream while this propagates.

sre-bot: Alert: continuous-batcher.hold_ms.p99 spiked from 20ms -> ~100ms across the canary cohort. Cohort alert triggered for tenant NM-22 (p99>2s). Related dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/continuous-batcher

tara: We should repro locally to validate config sensitivity. Repro steps for infra/qa: run a small prompt workload (prompt-size 8–12 tokens) at ~150 QPS with burst patterns. Example:

```python
# repro: simulate many tiny prompts to hit coalescer behavior
python tests/load_smallreqs.py --qps 150 --duration 120 --prompt-size 10 --burst-interval 5
```

Set client header to normal (no nobatch) to exercise coalescer.

maria: Update: after flipping the tenant flag to bypass coalescing for NM-22, p99 dropped from 4.8s -> ~720ms within ~30s. Support, can you confirm with NimbusMaps?

support: NimbusMaps confirmed improvement and says throughput/latency looks back to baseline. They're still seeing a few 500s though — looks like some client retries hammered upstream after a short window.

aj: Noted — auth team reported a transient auth token TTL mismatch at ~22:09 which produced a spike of 401s and immediate client retries. That retry storm likely amplified the coalescing effect. Looping in @ben-auth.

samir: OK, follow-ups: 1) revert default grace_ms to 20ms and keep canary small until we validate (ACTION aj), 2) make a permanent per-tenant nobatch feature and expose it to support (ACTION samir), 3) add per-tenant hold_ms p95/p99 to dashboards and set alerting (ACTION tara), 4) add runbook entry for "coalescer-induced p99" with quick mitigations (flags, per-tenant bypass, quick rollback) (ACTION maria).

maria: I'll draft the runbook and small post-incident doc. We'll include the repro script and the rbctl commands used.

sre-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (tenant bypass applied, default rolled toward baseline). Will auto-close if no regressions in 2 hours.

support: Customer says the UX is good now and will monitor. Closing the escalation on our side pending postmortem. Thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:
